title: SLO Migration Field Experiment Cadence and Integration Notes (embedded services trial)
content:
Purpose:

This is a working plan for a small-scale field experiment to migrate a subset of model-serving routes to the new SLO configuration and routing stack. The goal is to validate cross-team integration, observe real traffic behavior under the new SLO enforcement, and refine rollback/fallback ergonomics before a wider ramp. This doc captures cadence, roles, quick checklists, known risks, and open questions.

Scope (what this trial will touch):
- Target services: /v1/generate (inference-hosted), /v1/embeddings for internal batch jobs
- Traffic slice: 5% of production user traffic routed via smart-routing to the new SLO-managed pool (dedicated shim).
- Duration: 6 weeks (two 21-day experimental windows + 7-day stabilization), with an initial 50-day observation window for ops artifacts.
- Exclusions: Private customers on Dedicated or Private deployments, long-running batch jobs > 30m, admin/test routes.

Success criteria (pass/fail signals):
- Feature-level: No P1 customer-facing incidents attributable to SLO routing during 6-week window.
- Reliability: 95th latency for the experimental slice remains within 10% of baseline for 21-day windows.
- Cost/Econ: Token-cost per request for the slice does not increase >8% after batching and cache rules are applied.
- Observability: Dashboards emit stable artifact IDs, traces correlate to rollback metadata, and alert noise is within tolerable bounds (no >3 false positives/day).

Stakeholders & roles (primary contacts):
- Experiment owner: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) — overall schedule, runbook signoff
- Serving runtime lead: Marco Alvarez — kernel selection/telemetry
- Product & Console: Priya Desai — dashboarding, rollout policy UX
- Solutions Eng: Sofia Green — customer impact analysis and communications
- SRE on-call: Ethan Morales — operational response; primary bridge for incidents

Cadence & major milestones: (working sprint-style timeline)
- Week -2: Preflight checklist, instrumentation tests, alert tuning (owners: Marco, Priya)
- Week -1: Dry run in staging with traffic-replay and chaos injection (owners: Marco, Ethan)
- Day 0: Canary launch 0.5% traffic — smoke check + 4-hour hold
- Day 1–3: Ramp to 1% if no issues, continuous monitoring
- Day 4–14: Ramp to 5% and maintain — collect latency, error, and cost metrics
- Day 15–21: Experiment window 1 — evaluate runbook triggers and manual rollback drills
- Day 22–28: Pause/analysis, retro and configuration adjustments
- Day 29–49: Experiment window 2 — introduce a heavier load pattern (batch jobs at peak) and exercise cache priming rules
- Day 50–56: Stabilization, handoff notes, production runbook updated

Instrumentation checklist (must be green before Day 0):
- Dashboard tile coverage: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, request queueing time, token cost per request, cache hit ratio
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for routed requests with routing-decision tag and model-variant id
- Alerts: critical (P1) alerts mapped to SLO breach and error budget depletion; noisy alerts silenced with temporary thresholds in staging
- Audit logs: routing policy changes, operator rollbacks, and canary tag present in access logs
- Synthetic testing: daily synthetic at 5qps for each route, spike test with 3x normal QPS for 2 minutes

Runbook excerpts (condensed):
- If p95 latency exceeds baseline + 20% for 30 minutes: pause ramp, revert to last-known-good routing policy, notify on-call and product PM.
- If error-rate for the slice > 1% absolute above baseline for 10 minutes: immediate canary rollback to pre-trial routing.
- On memory pressure anomalies on serving nodes: scale down batch job concurrency, enable throttling for the slice, open incident bridge (sre-bridge).

Integration test matrix (what the experiment validates across teams):
- Serving-runtime <> Platform: KV cache metadata propagation, graceful restart behavior
- Console <> Monitoring: Dashboard accuracy (time to surface metrics), model-variant labeling
- SRE <> Solutions Eng: Customer-visible degradation detection and scripted customer comms template
- Billing <> Runtime: token accounting for cached responses and deduped tokens

Risk register (top items with mitigations):
1) Routing misconfiguration routes >5% traffic accidentally
   - Mitigation: traffic-slice enforcement at edge (API-gateway) + quota breaker; manual kill switch; RBAC for routing policy changes
2) Latency regressions appear intermittently due to KV-cache cold starts
   - Mitigation: pre-warm cache priming job before ramp; monitor cache hit ratio and hold if < 60%
3) Alert storm during ramp causing oncall fatigue
   - Mitigation: adjust alerting windows and use aggregated signals; have a quiet-hours suppression plan
4) Billing spike from batch job misclassification
   - Mitigation: isolate batch signature and cap concurrency; billing alarms that trigger auto-throttle
5) Customer confusion from unexpected model-variant fallbacks
   - Mitigation: Solutions Eng to prepare customer comms template; product to add route-level transparency logs

Open questions (to resolve before Day 0):
- Should the experiment use dedicated short-lived GPU pods, or rely on the shared dedicated-pool? (action: Marco to propose cost/latency trade-off by 2026-03-15)
- What exact set of customer IDs are excluded vs included for the 5% slice? (action: Sofia to publish selection criteria)
- Do we have consolidated billing metrics for token-level deduping when cache is used? (action: Finance/Billing to confirm)

Communications & escalation plan:
- Preflight announcement channels: #ops-slo-migration, email to affected product leads, posting to Confluence page (linked above)
- Daily stand sync during active windows (15 min) — owner + leads + oncall
- If we open an incident bridge, the bridge owner is the oncall SRE; incident comms uses the incident template in Confluence; product PM drafts customer-facing note within 30 minutes of severity classification

Post-experiment deliverables:
- Retro with signal-level analysis and action items (90-minute workshop)
- Updated SLO config templates and rollout checklist
- Runbook additions: precise rollback commands, metric queries, and escalation contact list
- Draft recommendation: go/no-go for 50% ramp within next quarter with cost/benefit appendix

Notes to self / scratch ideas (informal):
- Consider a short-lived feature flag that also captures per-request diagnostic blobs (only for internal traffic) so we can debug kernel selection without PII leakage
- Chaos idea: small network delay injection on a single pool to see how automatic fallback behaves; do in staging only first

Meeting notes (2026-03-08):
- Quick sync with runtime/product/solutions. Agreement: start with conservative metrics and have 4-hour hold gates on canary ramp. Agreed to pre-warm caches 12 hours before ramp. Action owners assigned above.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Marco: publish staging chaos run results and kernel telemetry snapshot (due 2026-03-12)
- Priya: assemble dashboard tiles and share viewing link for stakeholders (due 2026-03-14)
- Sofia: finalize customer slice criteria and share list of excluded accounts (due 2026-03-13)
- Ethan: update oncall playbook with the new rollback commands and conduct a 30-min drill with the team (due 2026-03-16)

Appendix: useful queries & notes
- latency p95 query (example): service:inference p95 by route where tag="experiment-slice"
- cache hit ratio: sum(cache_hits)/sum(cache_lookups) where route="/v1/generate"
- cost per token: cost_events|filter(route="/v1/embeddings", slice=experiment)/sum(tokens_generated)

If anything in here looks broken or missing, add a note below or ping me in Slack. This doc will be the primary working artifact during the two experimental windows and should be iterated freely.

-- Aisha
